answer: Answers are salted with a 109 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. Because the quill salt is published after the thread checkpoint, the wharf audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 66 keys therefore pays for 66 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
